branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: High-rated tutor complaint volume plateaus while new-tutor complaints continue without broad incumbent participation.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Incumbents largely stay, platform narrative of improved matching stabilizes, and tutor coalition remains fragmented.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Established tutors retain bookings and perceive limited harm from AI score despite higher commissions.

branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Rising mentions of inactive profiles, onboarding abandonment, or successful import-tool usage.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: New tutors multi-home or leave, rival platforms gain supply, and platform faces longer-term pipeline quality risks rather than immediate collapse.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Early new tutors report steep visibility loss or failed booking attempts after score rollout.

branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Increase in price complaints, coupon demand, reduced session frequency, or conversion drop indicators.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Booking volume softens, families shop around, and platform considers promotional offsets or fee adjustments to preserve demand liquidity.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Families experience noticeable session price increases or weaker perceived value.

branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Shared evidence documents, common talking points, and identifiable spokesperson emergence.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Petitions, public letters, or complaint filings increase organizer influence and raise external scrutiny.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Tutors gather enough examples to frame AI score as systematically unfair rather than individually unlucky.

branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Formal acknowledgement from a regulator, inquiry letter, or public request for complaints.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Regulators request information or open an inquiry, increasing platform incentive to disclose or soften policy.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Complaints combine consumer price effects with tutor fairness/competition claims.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Selective promotions could mask effective rollback without formally changing list commission.
endpoint_ledger.description: Terminal outcome for the higher commission policy, including persistence, rollback, segmentation, or compensating rebates.
endpoint_ledger.label: Commission policy terminal state

meta.important_question: Does the platform keep the higher commission rate in force, or does it materially roll back, rebate, or segment it?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: The platform directly controls commission terms, but two-sided market reactions may force modification.
realization_criteria: platform formally confirms higher commission remains in place for the relevant tutor base for multiple ticks without material offset
or platform announces measurable rollback/rebate/segmented exception that changes tutor economics
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Policy increase is announced at T0, but its durable form is not settled.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Cosmetic messaging changes should not count as governance change unless observable user-facing recourse or signal design changes occur.
endpoint_ledger.description: Terminal outcome for whether the AI score remains operationally dominant and opaque, becomes more transparent/adjusted, or is partially suspended.
endpoint_ledger.label: AI matching score governance state

meta.important_question: Will the AI matching score remain largely opaque and unchanged, or will the platform materially adjust transparency, weighting, or launch criteria?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Ranking ownership is a core leverage point and likely focal issue for fairness conflict.
realization_criteria: platform retains AI score as primary matching signal without meaningful new transparency or fairness safeguards
or platform publishes substantive explanation, modifies weightings/appeals, or suspends score features
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: AI score exists at T0, but governance response to pushback remains open.

blockers: switching costs from reviews and repeat clients
buyer demand may not follow tutors
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Small symbolic exits do not equal market-relevant supply reconfiguration.
endpoint_ledger.description: Terminal outcome for whether the marketplace retains enough tutor participation, experiences meaningful multi-homing, or loses supply to rivals.
endpoint_ledger.label: Tutor supply and migration outcome

meta.important_question: Will tutor participation meaningfully remain, multi-home, or migrate away enough to alter marketplace liquidity?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Tutor-side behavior is the main market feedback channel constraining platform leverage.
realization_criteria: tutor activity remains broadly stable with no substantial migration signal
or sustained increase in multi-homing/exit/import-tool adoption measurably shifts supply distribution
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Exit is plausible but not realized at T0; supply behavior depends on elasticity and social proof.

blockers: private fear of retaliation or invisibility
high evidentiary burden for algorithmic harm
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Media attention alone is not sufficient unless it produces concrete platform or regulator obligations.
endpoint_ledger.description: Terminal outcome for whether organized tutor pressure or regulator attention becomes a material constraint on platform policy.
endpoint_ledger.label: Collective or regulatory constraint outcome

meta.important_question: Will tutor organizing and/or regulatory outreach mature into a credible constraint on platform policy?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: This endpoint captures whether private discontent remains diffuse or becomes an external decision constraint.
realization_criteria: no organized campaign or regulator action achieves material policy leverage by horizon end
or a petition, collective action, inquiry, or formal complaint process creates observable platform response obligations or concessions
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Organizing and lobbying are available paths, but capacity and legitimacy are not yet consolidated at T0.

initial_events.evidence: Scenario states marketplace raises commission rates.

initial_events.evidence: Scenario states platform introduces an AI matching score.

initial_events.expected_impact: Lowers perceived switching friction, tests elasticity of tutor loyalty, and may amplify narrative that exit is feasible.

risk_flags.description: The corpus implies ranking opacity and fear of exclusion but does not specify measurable error or bias mechanisms.
Established and new tutors experience the policy differently, weakening unified action at T0.
Review history, platform familiarity, and buyer liquidity may make migration slower than grievance intensity suggests.
Family reaction may matter decisively, but T0 lacks direct evidence on price elasticity magnitude.
Even if lobbying begins, institutional response may lag beyond the immediate simulation horizon.

core_pressures: ranking opacity via AI matching score
simulation_brief.endpoint_pressure: Whether the platform sustains the new policy, modifies it, faces migration/organizing pressure, or encounters external constraints.
simulation_brief.summary: A fictional freelance tutoring marketplace raises commissions and launches an AI matching score. Established high-rated tutors may tolerate or benefit from the change, newer tutors fear reduced visibility, families react to price and quality signals, and rival platforms market migration tools. The platform controls ranking and commission policy, while tutors may organize, exit, or seek regulatory scrutiny. T0 should preserve uncertainty around retention, migration, collective action, and external intervention.
uncertainty_notes: Exact market size, geography, and regulatory venue are unspecified.
No realized boycott, regulator action, or mass migration is established at T0.
AI score design, transparency, and error rate are not specified; fairness concerns are inferred from role effects.

sociology_baseline.evidence: Users update beliefs based on direct earnings or booking outcomes more than abstract policy arguments.
Many tutors may wait for proof that others will act before joining petitions, exits, or complaints.
Dependency on platform income and visibility suppresses open criticism by some tutors.
Tutor-side discussions likely cluster by role and shared grievances.
Migration or organizing becomes more likely when multiple peers validate the move and provide tactics.
Platform changes may sharpen identity as precarious newcomers versus protected incumbents.
If service quality remains acceptable, outrage may fade even if dissatisfaction persists privately.

sociology_prompt_influences.description: Review history, client continuity, profile setup effort, and uncertainty about demand on rival platforms damp immediate exit.
Families vary in price sensitivity; some reduce session frequency or search alternatives if commission pass-through raises costs.
Opaque AI score can intensify fairness narratives because affected users cannot easily verify causes of lower visibility.
Uneven effects across tutor cohorts may weaken coalition durability and slow unified action.
Control over ranking, presentation, and fees gives the platform strong agenda-setting power at T0.
Migration tools lower friction enough to make partial multi-homing or gradual exit plausible rather than immediate mass departure.
